rules.title: Valid document
rules.why: A Plan must parse as YAML and have a spec mapping, or the controller can't admit it.
rules.fix: Fix the YAML syntax; ensure top-level apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec are present and spec is a mapping.

rules.title: apiVersion
rules.why: Only agent.leartech.io/v1alpha1 is served by the platform CRD.
rules.fix: Set apiVersion: agent.leartech.io/v1alpha1.

rules.title: kind
rules.why: The catalog accepts only Plan and PlanTemplate.
rules.fix: Set kind to Plan or PlanTemplate.

rules.title: Name shape
rules.why: metadata.name becomes a DNS-1123 label and part of the child AgentRun name; >58 chars risks the 63-byte pod-label cap.
rules.fix: Use a lowercase DNS-1123 name (letters, digits, hyphens) of at most 58 characters.

rules.title: Hold-by-default
rules.why: A catalog Plan is a PROPOSAL — it must not execute on merge. Execution is a separate, human-gated promote/unpause.
rules.fix: Set spec.paused: true on every Plan.

rules.title: Step shape
rules.why: Each step is either a template include (use:) or a concrete step; a concrete non-fan-in step needs a kind and an agentType.
rules.fix: Give the step a name; for a concrete step set kind to pr|apply|check and set agentType; or make it a use:/fanIn step.

rules.title: Unique step names
rules.why: Step names must be unique — they compute the child AgentRun name and dependsOn edges.
rules.fix: Rename duplicate steps so every step name is unique.

rules.title: dependsOn resolves
rules.why: A dependsOn that names no declared step leaves the step permanently blocked.
rules.fix: Point dependsOn at existing step names, or remove the dangling entry.

rules.title: Template shape
rules.why: A PlanTemplate declares params and steps; its steps are concrete (kind+agentType) and must not nest use: (expansion is depth-1).
rules.fix: Give the template params + steps; make each step concrete (kind+agentType) with no nested use:.

rules.title: No laptop paths
rules.why: A Plan runs in a K8s Job with only the target repo checked out — laptop/absolute paths never resolve.
rules.fix: Reference only repo-committed or defined-store artifacts; remove /Users/, /home/, or ~/ paths.

rules.title: No cycle
rules.why: A dependsOn cycle makes the DAG un-runnable; the controller marks the Plan Failed.
rules.fix: Break the cycle so the dependsOn graph is acyclic.

rules.title: No self-dependency
rules.why: A step depending on itself (via dependsOn or triggeredWhen) can never start.
rules.fix: Remove the self-reference.

rules.title: Fan-in shape
rules.why: A fanIn step is a no-agent gate: it must fan in from >=1 dependsOn and assert >=1 fanInValidate path; a non-fan-in step must not set fanInValidate.
rules.fix: For fanIn: true add dependsOn + fanInValidate; otherwise remove fanInValidate.

rules.title: use-step fields
rules.why: A use: step must not smuggle runtime fields — the template supplies them; expansion hard-fails otherwise.
rules.fix: On a use: step keep only name, use, with, dependsOn (and triggeredWhen); remove agentType/inputs/repo/budgetIter/hold/fanIn/fanInValidate.

rules.title: Template resolvable
rules.why: A use: references a PlanTemplate; if it isn't in this PR it must already exist on the target cluster.
rules.fix: Co-submit the referenced template, or confirm it is deployed on the cluster.

rules.title: Required params
rules.why: A template param marked required must be supplied, or expansion fails.
rules.fix: Add the missing param(s) to the use-step's with: block.

rules.title: triggeredWhen
rules.why: triggeredWhen must name a declared step and a valid phase, or the trigger never fires.
rules.fix: Point triggeredWhen.step at an existing step and set phase to Running|AwaitingReview|AwaitingApproval|Succeeded.

rules.title: Expanded name length
rules.why: An over-long expanded child name (<plan>-<useStep>-<tmplStep>) is hash-truncated by the controller — it still runs but the name is unreadable.
rules.fix: Shorten the plan, use-step, or template step names to keep the expanded name under 57 chars.

rules.title: Test coherence
rules.why: test.directed vocabulary is kind-specific; a mismatch is a silent no-op, and a directive without spec.test is ignored.
rules.fix: Match test.directed to the step kind (pr→merged|closed_unmerged|opened, check→pass|fail, apply→succeed|error) and set spec.test: true.

rules.title: No unknown fields
rules.why: Fields not in the Plan/PlanTemplate CRD are strict-decoded out by the apiserver at apply, so a Plan carrying them cannot be instantiated. Common offenders: a step-level `goal` (belongs under `inputs`) and a spec-level `description` (not a CRD field).
rules.fix: Use only CRD fields. Put a step goal under `inputs:` (inputs.goal); drop spec-level `description` (use a YAML comment for human context).

rules.title: Inputs by agent type
rules.why: A step's inputs are consumed by the agent runtime, so they must match the agentType's contract or the agent Job fails at run time. Dev agents (go/ng/rust/py) consume an Initiative (name + goal + repo + branch, or a repos: list); the infra agent is action-driven (action + per-action fields), not goal-driven.
rules.fix: Dev steps: inputs {name, repo, branch, goal} (branch required for the legacy single-repo shape; or use repos:[{repo,branch}]). Infra steps: inputs {action, …} (e.g. release-health-check / chart-config). See AGENTS.md.

rules.title: Infra steps live in templates
rules.why: Infra steps (agentType leartech-agent-infra) are privileged, cross-cutting operations — release-verify, deploy-health, chart-config. In the PUBLIC catalog a plain Plan must not hand-author them: they belong in curated, OWNERS-gated PlanTemplates and are composed via use:. Hand-authored infra in a submitted Plan is a governance + security hole (a submitter declaring privileged infra work directly) and duplicates the standard verification the deployment path injects. Infra steps are allowed ONLY in kind: PlanTemplate.
rules.fix: Remove the infra step from the Plan and compose the right PlanTemplate via a use: step instead (e.g. `use: verify-release-flow`). If no template covers your need, propose a new PlanTemplate (which OWNERS review) rather than hand-authoring the infra step.

rules.title: verify-release-flow is auto-injected
rules.why: The platform auto-composes verify-release-flow after every deployable PR step (kind:pr carrying a repo), wired to the REAL merged PR (pr=${steps.<step>.pr}). A hand-authored `use: verify-release-flow` that dependsOn such a step therefore duplicates that injection — two verify-release-flow expansions — and typically also carries a broken hand-set sha. (A standalone verify-release-flow that does NOT dependsOn a PR step — verifying an already-deployed service by explicit sha — is legitimate and allowed.)
rules.fix: Remove the `use: verify-release-flow` step that dependsOn your PR step — the platform injects it on submission. Keep a hand-authored verify-release-flow only to verify a service NOT produced by a PR step in this Plan (and then supply an explicit commit sha).

rules.title: Resolvable commit sha
rules.why: A supplied `with.sha` must be a real commit sha (7–40 hex) so the release/verify checks can resolve the commit; a ref like HEAD or a branch name never resolves at check time and the check fails. With auto-injection you normally omit sha entirely — the injected verify uses the merged PR.
rules.fix: Set with.sha to a full commit sha (40 hex), or omit it and rely on the injected PR token. Do not use HEAD or a branch name.

rules.title: Verdict steps must be deterministic
rules.why: A kind: check step handed to a DEV agentType (go/ng/rust/py) cannot produce a deterministic verdict. A dev agent is a single LLM query() session: it exits 0 unless it crashes or hits max-turns, so a goal saying "FAIL (exit non-zero) if any assertion fails" is untrue — the runtime discards the verdict (see hub/status/agent-verdict-exit-code-fix-2026-08-05.md, still SPEC). Observed live: a verify step reported six of six assertions un-executed and verdict FAIL in prose while the session exited 0. Deterministic verification belongs on an infra agent with a canned action, which R22 requires be composed via use: a PlanTemplate.
rules.fix: Replace the hand-authored check with a `use:` step composing a PlanTemplate whose infra step uses a canned action (release-pipeline-status, promote-status, bootjob-for-commit, deploy-health). If no template covers the assertion, propose a new PlanTemplate (OWNERS-reviewed) rather than asserting it in a dev-agent goal.

rules.title: GitOps repo targets are template-only
rules.why: A step whose target repo is a cluster GitOps repo (jx-build-cluster-*) edits live helmfiles and JX-rendered config-root across the fleet — privileged infra work no matter which agentType runs it. R22 catches this only when the step declares an infra agentType, so a dev agent (e.g. leartech-agent-go) pointed at jx-build-cluster-gsm bypasses it. That is exactly the governance hole R22 exists to close, reached from the repo side rather than the agent side. A one-off GitOps decommission/enablement is operator work (needs-human:gitops-overlay); a recurring one belongs in an OWNERS-gated PlanTemplate.
rules.fix: Remove the GitOps step from the Plan. Compose the change via an OWNERS-gated infra PlanTemplate (use:), or have an operator apply it manually. A plain catalog Plan must not hand-author edits to jx-build-cluster-* repos.

rules.title: Goal-prose hazards
rules.why: The structural rules cannot see inside a step's free-text inputs.goal, so a hazardous instruction — today, editing the JX-rendered config-root tree — slips through. config-root/ is boot-rendered output; hand-editing it is always wrong because boot overwrites it, and a dev agent reads the goal literally. (Advisory warning — goal prose is heuristic, so this surfaces the hazard for human + ai-review rather than hard-gating.)
rules.fix: Do not instruct edits to config-root in a step goal. Edit the source (helmfile.yaml / .jx/gitops inputs) and let boot re-render config-root. If the goal merely warns against editing config-root, this is safe to ignore.
